clue.text: Superior bloomer, the ultimate from baker

parts.note: a bloomer is a blunder, a gaffe

indicators.note: the ultimate from a word is its very last letter, here of baker

explanation.surface: A boss baker's best loaf of bread, a bloomer, finished off by the last baker on shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like the bread loaf, but it is the slang word for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman, the person superior to the workers.

clue.text: Familiar mounted soldier loaded in explosives half-heartedly

indicators.note: loaded in means put inside, so the soldier goes into the shortened ammunition
half-heartedly means losing half of the doubled middle letters

parts.note: ammo, short for ammunition, covers explosives

indicators.note: mounted means put up, so in a down answer the soldier reads bottom to top

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A familiar cavalry soldier is loaded down with explosives, though without much enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar is a close friend, and the Spanish word for a friend is common in English.

clue.text: It's useless when chocolate figure's misshapen and rigid, as Cockney says

indicators.note: misshapen means bent out of form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word figure, the 's joining it to its anagram signal

indicators.note: Cockney speakers famously drop the H at the start of a word

parts.note: rigid means hard

explanation.surface: A chocolate figure that is misshapen and rigid is useless, a Cockney might say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As useful as a chocolate fireguard' is a British idiom for something hopeless; Cockney is the London dialect that drops H.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate screen in front of a hearth would melt, so the idiom names it as useless.

clue.text: Smelly, the French nettle bug?

parts.note: rank means foul-smelling
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A smelly French insect that lives on nettles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nettle bug' looks like a garden insect, but both words are verbs meaning to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to irritate or vex, just as nettle and bug both mean to annoy.

clue.text: No 1 might give staff this with mature beer to be knocked back

parts.note: to mature is to age

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, and here the word for the beer is turned back to front

parts.note: pils is a pale lager beer, short for pilsner

explanation.surface: The boss hands staff a slip, along with a mature beer to knock back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 1' follows on from 1 across: the gaffer, the boss, who gives staff their pay slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Employers issue each worker a pay statement, so the boss gives staff this document.

clue.text: Town broadcast film of top quality horse

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the film genre is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: a western is a cowboy film
super means excellent, of top quality
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A town is broadcasting a top-quality film about a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Weston-super-Mare is a seaside resort town in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somerset seaside resort is a large town on the Bristol Channel coast.

clue.text: Leaping dog entertains expert in church that circulates after meal

indicators.note: entertains means holds as a guest, so the dog's letters go around the rest
leaping means jumping up, so in a down answer the dog reads bottom to top

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog

indicators.note: in places the expert inside the church letters

parts.note: RC stands for the Roman Catholic church
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A jumping dog amuses an expert in a church where things go round after dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A grace cup is a loving cup of wine passed round the table after grace at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Paddy, Rio and Sydney perhaps turned up

indicators.note: turned up means flipped upward, so in a down answer the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro and Sydney are both ports, examples hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Three people, Paddy, Rio and Sydney, turned up together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like a name, but it is British slang for a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy and a strop are both British informal words for a sulky fit of bad temper.

clue.text: Up-to-date woman obtains wood treatment available here

parts.note: in means fashionable, up to date
fir is a softwood timber
Mary is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A trendy woman buys wood treatment, for sale here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood treatment' reads as varnish, but treatment is the definition's medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An infirmary is a hospital, a place where medical treatment is given.

clue.text: Somebody is heading west in Nissan for islands

indicators.note: in says the pieces go inside the car's name

parts.note: the Micra is a small Nissan car
somebody, anybody: one

indicators.note: in an across clue heading west means reading from right to left, so the little word is turned back

explanation.surface: Someone drives west in a Nissan, looking for islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Micronesia is a group of small island chains in the western Pacific.

clue.text: Artiste regularly checks fine cleavage

indicators.note: checks means stops or holds back, so the picked letters close around and hold the next piece
regularly means taking every other letter of the word artiste

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: A performer regularly checks a fine show of cleavage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleavage is a split or division, as is a rift between people or in rock.

clue.text: Dance contest's second round — girl's stifled by shout of disapproval

indicators.note: something stifled is smothered, so these letters are held inside the shout

parts.note: boo is the shout a crowd gives in disapproval

indicators.note: second picks the second letter of the word contest

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a round shape is an O

explanation.surface: In the second round of a dance contest, a girl is drowned out by booing.
explanation.definitionFit: The boogaloo is a 1960s style of dance to soul and Latin music.

clue.text: Large business representative visits republic

indicators.note: visits means goes inside, so the representative's letters go into the republic

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland
an MP, a Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: A sales representative from a big firm pays a visit to Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A business empire is a large group of companies under one owner.

clue.text: Some describe tattooed character in Marathon

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some runners describe the tattooed character they met at a marathon.
explanation.walkthrough: Marathon is a Greek place, so its characters are Greek letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, and Marathon is in Greece.

clue.text: Electronic work in Silicon Valley consumed complex

parts.note: Silicon Valley is in California, where Americans spell labour as labor
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Electronic work in Silicon Valley consumed a complicated project.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate means intricate and detailed, with many parts, just as complex does.

clue.text: Dick's vehicle Mark used around courtyard

indicators.note: around says the mark's letters enclose the courtyard

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
a quad is a quadrangle, a college courtyard

explanation.surface: A man called Dick parks his car, which Mark has used, around a courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dick' looks like a name, but it is old slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A dick is slang for a police detective, and a squad car is a police patrol car.

clue.text: Brother clutching old ticker conveys pessimistic view ahead

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so the brother's letters go around the old

parts.note: Dom is the title of a Benedictine monk, a religious brother
a ticker is slang for a watch

explanation.surface: A monk clutching an old heart passes on a gloomy forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ticker' looks like slang for the heart, but means a watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Doomwatch is close observation that expects disaster, a gloomy outlook on the future.

clue.text: Catholic college in rousing environment where resistance breaks out

indicators.note: in says the college letter goes inside
environment names the surrounding word that does the enclosing
resistance is R in physics, and breaking out means escaping from the word

parts.note: an electric atmosphere is rousing and thrilling

explanation.surface: A Catholic college in a thrilling setting where a resistance movement breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catholic' looks like the church, but here is the lower-case adjective meaning broad-ranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic with a small c means wide-ranging in tastes, the same as drawing from many sources.

clue.text: Horse race tips in Hindi given by better

indicators.note: given by means the next piece follows on after the first

parts.note: the two tips of the word Hindi are H and I, written out with the and joining them
to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: Racing tips printed in Hindi, given out by a punter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like a punter but is the verb meaning to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is a race in which horses carry different weights to even out their chances.

clue.text: Ring reportedly steals precious stone

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is heard rather than read, so the slang word for steals is spelt by its sound

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal

explanation.surface: A ring thief is said to have made off with a precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded semi-precious variety of chalcedony used in jewellery.

clue.text: Coin's occupying hole

parts.note: occupying means in a place
a vent is an opening or hole

explanation.surface: A coin is stuck in a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coin' is a verb here: to coin a word is to make it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin a phrase is to create it, to devise something new.

clue.text: The greatest sporting ego, potentially game's number one?

indicators.note: sporting means showing off or playing, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the boxer, called himself The Greatest

explanation.surface: The greatest boxer's sporting ego might make him the number one in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: In football the goalkeeper traditionally wears the number 1 shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: The keeper wears shirt number one, so a goalkeeper is potentially a team's number one.

clue.text: Musician's catalogue including Mozart's Third

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the catalogue's letters go around the pick

parts.note: a catalogue is a list

indicators.note: Third picks the third letter of the word Mozart

explanation.surface: A musician's catalogue of works includes Mozart's Third Symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian virtuoso pianist and composer of the Romantic era.

clue.text: Somewhere in Hants, old duke leaves room upset

indicators.note: leaves means these letters go out of the town's name

parts.note: Ringwood is a market town in Hampshire, abbreviated Hants, in southern England

explanation.surface: In a Hampshire town an old duke walks out of a room in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as the temper of the duke, but it is a noun: a physical disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset can be a bodily disorder, and this fungal skin infection is one such complaint.

clue.text: Retired generation breaking rules? It's less common

indicators.note: retired means gone back, so the whole is read in reverse
breaking means splitting apart, so the generation goes between the two letters

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for rule, so two of them are rules

explanation.surface: A retired generation that breaks the rules is a less common sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarer is the comparative of rare, meaning found less often.

clue.text: Welshman, the earliest on station platform

parts.note: Dai is a stock Welsh man's name, short for David

indicators.note: the earliest on a word is its first letter, here of station

explanation.surface: A Welshman is the first person waiting on the station platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform at one end of a hall for speakers.

clue.text: Flight officer welcomes overseas government politician

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the officer's letters hold the government

parts.note: tec is short for detective, a police officer
the Raj was British rule in India
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A flight officer greets a politician from a government abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A trajectory is the path an object follows through the air, its line of flight.

clue.text: Grappler's wrestling mostly clean on canvas

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas

indicators.note: wrestling means struggling, so the letters are twisted round
mostly means all but the last letter of the word clean

clue.text: Clothing soaked at the front in XXX, having shrunk

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the shortened number
